note: Second- and third-generation ALK inhibitors went into ALK-rearranged patients on EML4-ALK xenografts plus Ba/F3 and patient-derived cell panels built around crizotinib-resistance mutations; every track matched, and the cell panel later picked lorlatinib responders.
label: NSCLC (ALK inhibitors)

engagement.model: Ba/F3 EML4-ALK L1196M cells and crizotinib-resistant patient-derived lines
engagement.note: Alectinib (CH5424802) blocked EML4-ALK L1196M, the crizotinib gatekeeper mutant first sequenced from a relapsing patient, in Ba/F3 cells; no dosed-human readout yet.
engagement.short: Alectinib blocks L1196M gatekeeper in cells
engagement.quote: CH5424802 inhibited ALK L1196M, which corresponds to the gatekeeper mutation conferring common resistance to kinase inhibitors, and blocked EML4-ALK L1196M-driven cell growth.
engagement.judgement: The L1196M mutation itself came from a crizotinib-relapsing patient (Choi 2010), so the mutant was clinic-derived, but alectinib's activity against it was a prospective prediction for a member drug. Ba/F3 are engineered murine cells, so model_kind is ex_vivo rather than animal; the same track carries the patient-derived crizotinib-resistant lines used from 2014. model_filed is true on the strength of the ceritinib, brigatinib and lorlatinib FDA reviews, which all describe Ba/F3 ALK-mutant panels; the alectinib review's L1196M line was not verified word by word.

engagement.model: Ba/F3 EML4-ALK L1196M cells and crizotinib-resistant patient-derived lines
engagement.note: Patient-derived crizotinib-resistant lines and Ba/F3 mutants said ceritinib engages L1196M, G1269A, I1171T and S1206Y ALK; crizotinib-pretreated patients responded 56% in ASCEND-1.
engagement.quote: Altogether, our results demonstrate that ceritinib can overcome crizotinib resistance, consistent with clinical data showing marked efficacy of ceritinib in patients with crizotinib-resistant disease.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Europe PMC full-text fetch returned HTTP 500); PMID 24675041, epub 2014-03-27.
engagement.magnitude_basis: mutant-ALK inhibition in cells versus objective response in crizotinib-pretreated patients
engagement.judgement: No trial measured tumour pALK in dosed humans, so the engagement readout is the response of crizotinib-resistant (mutant-ALK) patients, downstream of the target; this follows the atlas convention used for EGFR T790M. The patient side is ASCEND-1 (Shaw 2014, 10.1056/NEJMoa1311107, print 2014-03-27, NCT01283516 results posted 2014-08-11): ORR 56% in 80 crizotinib-pretreated patients, 'Responses were observed in patients with various resistance mutations in ALK and in patients without detectable mutations.' The same paper predicted G1202R and F1174C would escape, and found G1202R in 5 of 11 ceritinib-resistant biopsies; that patient-level half is scored under efficacy.

engagement.model: Ba/F3 EML4-ALK L1196M cells and crizotinib-resistant patient-derived lines
engagement.note: Ceritinib-resistant patient-derived lines said ALK-mutant tumours stay lorlatinib-sensitive and mutation-free ones do not; after second-generation TKIs, ORR was 62% versus 32%.
engagement.short: ALK mutations predicted lorlatinib response, 62% vs 32%
engagement.quote: In contrast, in patients who had failed 1 or more second-generation ALK TKIs, objective response rate was higher among patients with ALK mutations (62% v 32% [plasma]; 69% v 27% [tissue]).
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; PMID 30892989, epub 2019-03-20. The registry results record (NCT01970865, 2018-05-29) does not carry the mutation subgroup, so the comparison dates from the 2019 paper.
engagement.magnitude_basis: cell-line sensitivity by ALK-mutation status versus ORR by ALK-mutation status
engagement.reason: Mutant-ALK engagement predicted, then matched twice
engagement.judgement: Gainor 2016 (10.1158/2159-8290.CD-16-0596, epub 2016-07-18) made the prediction prospectively in ceritinib-resistant patient-derived lines ('the presence of ALK resistance mutations is highly predictive for sensitivity to lorlatinib, whereas those cell lines without ALK mutations are resistant'); Shaw 2019 tested it on 198 patients from the registrational phase 2 and states the comparison itself. Plasma-genotyped PFS was only HR 0.81, tissue-genotyped PFS HR 0.47; scored as a directional match. The L1198F resensitisation case (Shaw 2016, 10.1056/NEJMoa1508887) is the same system used at patient level, but the drug it predicted for was crizotinib, not a member, so it is not scored.

dose.model: EML4-ALK NSCLC xenografts (H2228/H3122, subcutaneous and intracranial)
dose.note: H2228 and Karpas-299 xenografts regressed on oral CH5424802; no human exposure to set against the regressing dose yet.
dose.short: Xenografts regress; no human exposure yet
dose.quote: Our results support the potential for clinical evaluation of CH5424802 for the treatment of patients with ALK-driven tumors.
dose.judgement: H2228/H3122 xenografts were used for crizotinib from 2007, but crizotinib is not a member; model_first_use_year is the first member (alectinib) in the system. The regressing mouse dose in Sakamoto 2011 was not read (abstract only), so the opener states no exposure target.

dose.model: EML4-ALK NSCLC xenografts (H2228/H3122, subcutaneous and intracranial)
dose.note: Crizotinib-resistant H2228 xenografts regressed at 50–100 mg/kg ceritinib, about 1–2.5× the human AUC at 750 mg; ASCEND-1 reached that dose (MTD) with 58% ORR.
dose.short: Regressing exposure reached at 750 mg MTD
dose.quote: LDK378 plasma exposures at 50 and 100 mg/kg were approximately 1.3 and 2.5 fold higher than those achieved in humans at the recommended dose, respectively.
dose.confidence_note: Review read in part (pharmacology and toxicology sections); the review also states 50 mg/kg gave 'exposures approximately equal to those achieved in humans' and complete regression in the I1171T model.
dose.magnitude_basis: mouse AUC at the regressing dose versus human AUC at 750 mg once daily
dose.judgement: Target reached and drug worked, so same. No clean tolerability margin was stated: rat biliopancreatic duct necrosis appeared at 5% and pancreatic atrophy at 1.5× the human AUC, and in the clinic 750 mg was the MTD with GI-driven dose reductions in most patients (FDA summary review) — that harm is counted once, under safety, where the animals predicted it. The review's own caveat that 'higher LDK378 exposures may be necessary to inhibit crizotinib-resistant tumors' is noted; ASCEND-8 later showed 450 mg fed is exposure-equivalent, which is later knowledge and does not change the status.

dose.model: EML4-ALK NSCLC xenografts (H2228/H3122, subcutaneous and intracranial)
dose.note: Xenograft Ceff 150 ng/mL (>80% G1202R growth inhibition) set 100 mg QD, the lowest dose above it; CNS effects capped 150–200 mg; ORR 48%.
dose.quote: The Ceff of 150 ng/mL was the concentration predicted to result in >80% tumor growth inhibition of the ALK G1202R resistance mutation.
dose.confidence_note: Review read in part (nonclinical summary, RP2D selection); phase 1 is Shaw 2017 (10.1016/S1470-2045(17)30680-0), no MTD identified, one DLT at 200 mg.
dose.magnitude_basis: steady-state exposure at 100 mg once daily versus the xenograft-derived Ceff of 150 ng/mL
dose.reason: Xenograft exposure targets reached and tolerated
dose.judgement: Zou 2015 (10.1016/j.ccell.2015.05.010) stated 'high selectivity and safety margins in a variety of preclinical studies', so margin_stated is true; it held only narrowly — neurocognitive effects at 150–200 mg pushed the RP2D down to the lowest dose that still exceeded Ceff, and no patient at 100 mg needed a dose reduction in dose-finding. Scored same rather than contra because the target was reached without the toxicity at that dose (decision 16); a stricter reading of the thin window would be same with source_calls_it partial.

dose.model: PBPK (Simcyp/GastroPlus) drug-interaction models used to set CYP3A co-medication dose adjustments
dose.note: Sponsor and FDA PBPK models extrapolated single-dose ketoconazole/rifampin DDIs to steady state; the one-third dose cut and the moderate-modulator study waiver rest on the model.
dose.short: PBPK sets ceritinib CYP3A dose rule
dose.quote: Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling (PBPK) predicted that ketoconazole can increase the steady-state ceritinib exposure (AUC) by 51%; rifampin can decrease steady-state ceritinib AUC by 67%.
dose.confidence_note: FDA text bundle, 205755 ClinPharmR (lines 447-449, 1503-1536, Table 21). The steady-state prediction was never tested clinically; the reviewer judged a moderate CYP3A modulator trial unnecessary on the predicted magnitudes, which is regulator reliance on the model (the draft's context-level regulatory_reliance flag may need revisiting).
dose.judgement: Opening entry at the first member whose review used a PBPK DDI model; no observed steady-state DDI existed to compare, so untested. Healthy-subject single-dose DDI data informed the model rather than tested it.
dose.population: healthy subjects (single-dose ketoconazole and rifampin DDI studies) extrapolated to ALK-positive NSCLC patients at steady state

dose.model: PBPK (Simcyp/GastroPlus) drug-interaction models used to set CYP3A co-medication dose adjustments
dose.note: Simulated posaconazole AUC ratio 1.64 (1.31-2.25) vs observed 1.75 (1.57-1.95), 17 healthy subjects; rifampicin on M4 under-predicted; CYP2C8 DDI study waived on the model.
dose.quote: Can the integrated alectinib-M4 PBPK models predict the effect of CYP3A modulators on the PK of alectinib and M4? Yes.
dose.confidence_note: FDA text bundle, 208434 ClinPharmR OCP PBPK review (section 4.1, Tables 2-3, section 4.3). Healthy-volunteer DDI studies NP28990 (posaconazole, n=17) and NP29042 (rifampicin, n=24) have no registry record located, so registry_date is null. The default rifampicin model under-predicted induction and the M4 rifampicin ratios were called 'not satisfactory'; the parent-drug prediction is what the label rests on.
dose.judgement: An in-silico exposure prediction checked by the regulator against observed human exposure change: the parent AUC ratio was within 2x, so same, with the metabolite miss recorded as partial. Dose cell because the comparison governs a dosing recommendation (no CYP3A adjustment for alectinib; CYP2C8 study waived), not efficacy. Class-level: the model speaks to the drug's exposure, not to which patients respond.
dose.magnitude_basis: alectinib AUC ratio with posaconazole, simulated 1.64 vs observed 1.75 (study NP28990)
dose.population: healthy subjects, single 300 mg alectinib with posaconazole (NP28990) or rifampicin (NP29042)

dose.model: PBPK (Simcyp/GastroPlus) drug-interaction models used to set CYP3A co-medication dose adjustments
dose.note: FDA's own lorlatinib PBPK model reproduced the itraconazole single-dose DDI (B7461012) and set the 75 mg reduced dose with strong CYP3A inhibitors in the label.
dose.short: FDA PBPK reproduces itraconazole DDI, sets 75 mg
dose.quote: The model could also adequately predict the observed increased exposure of lorlatinib when a single 100 mg dose of lorlatinib was administered concomitantly following multiple dosing of 200 mg QD itraconazole (strong CYP3A inhibitor).
dose.confidence_note: FDA text bundle, 210868 MultidisciplineR (lines 4396-4406; PBPK review executive summary lines 10786-10795; itraconazole table near lines 11079-11110; Table 101 is the midazolam perpetrator check, predicted/observed 0.94-1.43). B7461012 is a healthy-volunteer DDI study; registry record not looked up, registry_date null. The steady-state 75 mg recommendation itself was never tested clinically.
dose.judgement: Second regulator-stated match on the same track, so strengthens rather than a new status. Magnitude is the regulator's 'adequately predict' plus the midazolam ratios within 1.5x, not an independent recomputation of the itraconazole ratio.
dose.reason: Regulator PBPK matched observed DDI twice
dose.magnitude_basis: lorlatinib exposure with itraconazole, PBPK-predicted vs observed (study B7461012, PBPK review lines 11079-11110); perpetrator check on midazolam Table 101 predicted/observed 0.94-1.43
dose.population: healthy subjects, single 100 mg lorlatinib with itraconazole 200 mg QD (B7461012); extrapolated to steady state in patients

efficacy.model: EML4-ALK NSCLC xenografts (H2228/H3122, subcutaneous and intracranial)
efficacy.note: EML4-ALK H2228 and NPM-ALK Karpas-299 xenografts regressed on alectinib (CH5424802), the first member in this model; no patient result yet.
efficacy.quote: Our results support the potential for clinical evaluation of CH5424802 for the treatment of patients with ALK-driven tumors.
efficacy.judgement: The class-level prediction (ALK-fusion tumours regress on a selective ALK inhibitor) was already supported in patients by crizotinib (2010), a non-member; this strip scores only the member drugs, so the track opens untested at the first member's xenograft paper.

efficacy.model: EML4-ALK NSCLC xenografts (H2228/H3122, subcutaneous and intracranial)
efficacy.note: AF-001JP primary endpoint: 43 of 46 crizotinib-naive ALK-rearranged patients responded (93.5%) at 300 mg BID, as H2228 xenograft regression predicted.
efficacy.quote: In the phase 2 portion of the study, 46 patients were treated with the recommended dose, of whom 43 achieved an objective response (93.5%, 95% CI 82.1-98.6) including two complete responses (4.3%, 0.5-14.8) and 41 partial responses (89.1%, 76.4-96.4).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; PMID 23639470, epub 2013-04-30. Registered at JapicCTI-101264, not ClinicalTrials.gov, so no registry results date.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft regression versus objective response rate

patient_trials.quote: Among 114 patients with NSCLC who received at least 400 mg of ceritinib per day, the overall response rate was 58% (95% confidence interval [CI], 48 to 67).
All eight crizotinib-naive patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC had a confirmed objective response (100% [63-100]).
As compared with crizotinib, alectinib showed superior efficacy and lower toxicity in primary treatment of ALK-positive NSCLC.

efficacy.judgement: A pairing: Seto 2013 does not itself set the xenograft beside the response rate (it cites alectinib only as 'a potent, selective, and orally available ALK inhibitor'), so comparison_stated is false and Sakamoto 2011 is the model side. First prospective member comparison; ceritinib's ASCEND-1 (2014) and brigatinib's phase 1/2 (2016) repeat it without changing status. outcome_tested is positive on the later PFS trials (ALEX HR 0.47, CROWN HR 0.28), both after this entry's date.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 EML4-ALK L1196M cells and crizotinib-resistant patient-derived lines
efficacy.note: Cells said ceritinib works on most crizotinib-resistant tumours but not G1202R/F1174C; patients responded regardless of mutation status and G1202R appeared in 5/11 ceritinib-resistant biopsies.
efficacy.short: Cells called who resists ceritinib: G1202R
efficacy.quote: However, we observed that ceritinib did not overcome two crizotinib-resistant ALK mutations, G1202R and F1174C, and one of these mutations was identified in 5 of 11 biopsies from patients with acquired resistance to ceritinib.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the patient side is a resistance-biopsy enrichment and the ASCEND-1 mutation-status responses (Shaw 2014), not a response rate by G1202R status.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: cell-line sensitivity by ALK genotype versus patient responses and resistance-biopsy genotypes
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level track: the cells predicted that ceritinib would work across crizotinib-resistant tumours, mutant or not (incomplete crizotinib inhibition), except G1202R/F1174C. ASCEND-1 found responses 'regardless of the presence of resistance mutations in ALK', and G1202R was enriched in ceritinib-resistant biopsies — both as predicted, but the G1202R half is a resistance correlation rather than a trial endpoint, so endpoint_role is null and confidence medium. A stricter reader could call the cell panel non-discriminating for the response question and score untested.

efficacy.model: EML4-ALK NSCLC xenografts (H2228/H3122, subcutaneous and intracranial)
efficacy.note: Intracranial H2228 model said alectinib beats crizotinib in brain; ALEX primary endpoint PFS HR 0.47 versus crizotinib, with CNS activity (abstract-level).
efficacy.short: Alectinib beat crizotinib as intracranial model said
efficacy.quote: As compared with crizotinib, alectinib showed superior efficacy and lower toxicity in primary treatment of ALK-positive NSCLC.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; PMID 28586279, epub 2017-06-06. The CNS-progression figures (12% vs 45%) are from memory of the full paper, not verified here, and are not relied on.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: intracranial xenograft growth inhibition versus progression-free survival hazard ratio

patient_trials.quote: Of 21 patients with CNS metastases at baseline, 11 (52%) had an objective response

In an interim analysis of results among patients with previously untreated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC, those who received lorlatinib had significantly longer progression-free survival and a higher frequency of intracranial response than those who received crizotinib.

efficacy.judgement: The model side is the FDA alectinib pharmacology review: 'Alectinib also showed greater inhibition of tumor growth than crizotinib in a mouse model implanted intracranially with the NCI-H2228 cell line'; ALEX is the first randomised head-to-head on its primary endpoint. Gadgeel 2014 (52% CNS responses in crizotinib-resistant patients) was the earlier single-arm signal but on a secondary endpoint. Zou 2015 made the same brain-metastasis prediction for lorlatinib and CROWN (2020) matched it; both are listed, not scored, because the status does not change. The NCT01588028 registry query returned an empty body and was not retried.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 EML4-ALK L1196M cells and crizotinib-resistant patient-derived lines
efficacy.note: Patient-derived cell panel said ALK mutations mark lorlatinib sensitivity after second-generation TKIs; ORR 62% vs 32%, tissue-genotyped PFS HR 0.47.
efficacy.short: Mutation-positive patients responded, as cells predicted
efficacy.quote: In patients who have failed 1 or more second-generation ALK TKIs, lorlatinib shows greater efficacy in patients with ALK mutations compared with patients without ALK mutations.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Plasma-genotyped PFS did not separate (HR 0.81); tissue genotyping did (HR 0.47); ORR separated on both.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: cell-line sensitivity by ALK-mutation status versus ORR and PFS by ALK-mutation status
efficacy.reason: Xenografts and mutant cells both matched
efficacy.judgement: Prospective: Gainor 2016 (patient-derived, ceritinib-resistant lines) preceded the registrational phase 2 analysis. The biomarker analysis was exploratory, not the trial's primary endpoint, so endpoint_role is null. The model also predicted no difference by mutation status after crizotinib alone, and none was found. In later knowledge, the ALK-mutation-guided choice of lorlatinib became the standard clinical use of this cell panel, which is why the track is scored at patient level.

efficacy.model: Patient-derived organoids from ALK-rearranged NSCLC scored by the CODRP growth-rate/stage-weighted index
efficacy.note: PDOs from eight lung-cancer patients (five ALK-positive) dosed with crizotinib, alectinib and brigatinib; the conventional AUC readout did not separate ALK-positive from ALK-negative organoids.
efficacy.short: ALK organoids built; AUC readout fails
efficacy.quote: We tested PDOs from eight patients with lung cancer to verify the CODRP index.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC10664561, PMID 37993887, J Exp Clin Cancer Res 42:309, published 2023-11-22). Opening entry at the system's first use for this class; the comparison is in the same paper.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use. Members alectinib and brigatinib were in the panel (crizotinib is not a member).
efficacy.population: ALK-rearranged NSCLC, Catholic University of Korea hospitals (surgical tissue and malignant pleural effusion)

efficacy.model: Patient-derived organoids from ALK-rearranged NSCLC scored by the CODRP growth-rate/stage-weighted index
efficacy.note: Four ALK-positive patients (two alectinib PR, two brigatinib PR/SD) were all called sensitive by the CODRP index; the AUC index alone had not separated them.
efficacy.quote: The proposed CODRP index-based drug sensitivity test classified ALK-targeted drug responses according to ALK rearrangement status and was verified to be consistent with the clinical drug treatment response.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Only four ALK-positive patients treated with a member drug, all responders (RECIST PR/SD), so no non-responder tested the index. The CODRP index weights AUC by clinical stage and organoid growth rate and was introduced after the plain AUC readout misclassified ALK-positive organoids; the paper's Methods do not state whether organoid testing preceded the clinical response.
efficacy.judgement: Organoids were compared with RECIST responses already on record: retrodiction, so retro not same. Scored on the paper's stated index; had the conventional AUC readout been the prediction this would be contra, which is why confidence is low. Patient-level: the system claims to pick responders, not to validate the class.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: organoid sensitive/resistant call vs RECIST 1.1 response, 4 of 4 concordant (alectinib x2, brigatinib x2)
efficacy.population: ALK-rearranged NSCLC patients treated with alectinib or brigatinib (n=4 compared)

efficacy.model: Patient-derived xenografts from ALK-rearranged NSCLC patients progressing on lorlatinib (MATCH-R, Gustave Roussy)
efficacy.note: PDXs grown from progression biopsies of lorlatinib-resistant MATCH-R patients (MR57; MR135 at two sites); cell lines were then derived from the PDXs.
efficacy.quote: A PDX model was developed from this first site of progression (R1) and a patient derived cell line was established (MR135-R1).
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6942925, PMID 31585938; Clin Cancer Res epub 2019-10-04, print 26(1):242, 2020). MATCH-R is NCT02517892 (biopsy protocol, no results posted), so registry_date is null. Opening entry at first use; the comparison is in the same paper.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the first PDX built from a patient progressing on a member drug; no earlier ALK PDX dosed with a member was found.
efficacy.population: ALK-rearranged NSCLC progressing on lorlatinib, MATCH-R prospective biopsy study (NCT02517892)

efficacy.model: Patient-derived xenografts from ALK-rearranged NSCLC patients progressing on lorlatinib (MATCH-R, Gustave Roussy)
efficacy.note: MR135-R2 PDX from an adrenal metastasis progressing on lorlatinib was not controlled by lorlatinib alone, as in the patient; NF2 loss, rescued by mTOR inhibition.
efficacy.quote: treatment of MR135-R2 PDX tumor-bearing mice with the combination was significantly more effective than with single agents in controlling tumor growth.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. One PDX in vivo; the lorlatinib-alone result is read from the combination comparison, not from a stated growth number. In the same paper the PDX-derived MR57-S cell line from another lorlatinib-progressing patient stayed lorlatinib-sensitive (IC50 50 nM), which the authors leave unexplained (possible drug withdrawal during derivation).
efficacy.judgement: PDX built from a progression biopsy after the clinic knew the patient was resistant: retrodiction. In vivo it reproduced the resistance, so retro. The discordant MR57-S result is a PDX-derived cell line, which is the same system as the draft's patient-derived resistant lines (alk-mutant-cells) and is flagged for that track rather than scored here.
efficacy.reason: PDX regrows on lorlatinib like patient
efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour growth under lorlatinib alone in the PDX vs RECIST progression on lorlatinib in the patient
efficacy.population: ALK-rearranged NSCLC patient MR135 progressing on lorlatinib (NF2 loss-of-function)

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 EML4-ALK L1196M cells and crizotinib-resistant patient-derived lines
efficacy.note: Mutant-cell panel ranked brigatinib above alectinib after crizotinib; ALTA-3 head-to-head found identical PFS (19.3 vs 19.2 months, HR 0.97), futility met.
efficacy.short: Cells ranked brigatinib over alectinib; trial tied
efficacy.quote: Brigatinib was not superior to alectinib for PFS in crizotinib-pretreated ALK+ NSCLC.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 37574132, epub 2023-08-12). Model side: Zhang 2016 abstract (PMID 27780853) and brigatinib FDA multidisciplinary review Study ARP618 Table 4 (figure, not text-extractable). ALTA-3 did not select by ALK resistance mutation; only 34% had ctDNA-detectable ALK fusion.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: predicted brigatinib superiority over alectinib across crizotinib-resistant ALK mutants versus BIRC-assessed PFS HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.66-1.42)
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison: Zhang 2016 states brigatinib 'exhibited a superior inhibitory profile compared with crizotinib, ceritinib, and alectinib at clinically achievable concentrations' in the same Ba/F3 mutant panel (ARP618) filed with the NDA; ALTA-3 then tested brigatinib against alectinib for superiority after crizotinib and found none. A prospective within-class ranking miss on this patient-level track, scored contra (one drug comparison's contra beats earlier same). Open rule question whether a member-vs-member ranking belongs in efficacy; the trial was not enriched for ALK mutations, so a reader could call the panel's prediction untested in this population.

safety.note: IND-enabling rat and monkey toxicology existed when ceritinib entered patients in January 2011; no comparison was public.
safety.quote: A Phase I, Multi-center, Open Label Dose Escalation Study of LDK378, Administered Orally in Adult Patients With Tumors Characterized by Genetic Abnormalities in Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase (ALK)
safety.confidence_note: Proxy opener: the registry record (first posted 2011-01-26, start 2011-01-24) evidences that first-in-human dosing, and therefore the toxicology package, existed; the toxicology itself was first described publicly in the 2014 FDA review.
safety.judgement: The brief allows a proxy for the opener. The quote is the registry's official title, which supports only that the model existed, not any prediction.

safety.note: Rat and monkey flagged GI tract, liver, pancreas and lung (phospholipidosis); patients showed GI toxicity, hepatotoxicity, pneumonitis/ILD, lipase rises and hyperglycaemia.
safety.short: GI, liver, lung harms predicted and seen
safety.quote: Gastrointestinal toxicity and hepatotoxicity were observed clinically and are included in the Warnings and Precautions section of the label for ceritinib.
safety.confidence_note: Review read in part; it also states lung phospholipidosis and macrophage aggregates 'correlate with pneumonitis and interstitial lung disease observed clinically', and hERG plus monkey QTc prolongation matched clinical QTc prolongation.
safety.magnitude_basis: target organs in rat and monkey versus labelled warnings
safety.judgement: Every labelled ceritinib harm the species could show was flagged in animals, mostly at or below the clinical exposure (biliopancreatic duct necrosis at 5% of human AUC). Convulsions seen clinically were unattributable (brain metastases) and the CNS safety pharmacology was clean; not scored as a miss. Bradycardia, a labelled class warning, was not found in the animal sections read, so its prediction is unverified.

safety.note: Alectinib: rat/monkey GI and lung haemorrhage, liver findings and monkey heart-rate fall preceded clinical ILD, hepatotoxicity, GI events and bradycardia; phototoxicity seen in vitro.
safety.quote: In the repeat dose toxicology study, monkeys treated at the high dose level also displayed decreases in heart rate at the end of the dosing phase, consistent with bradycardia reported in clinical trials.
safety.confidence_note: Review read in part. The clinical CPK rise/myalgia signal (grade 3 CPK increases in Seto 2013) was not found in the animal sections read; whether rats or monkeys showed skeletal-muscle findings is unverified.
safety.magnitude_basis: target organs and safety-pharmacology findings versus labelled warnings
safety.judgement: Registry date is NP28761 (NCT01871805) results, the first alectinib pivotal record posted. Rat tooth and bone findings were not seen in adults; the review itself assigns them to a paediatric population, so they are not scored as an over-prediction. hERG inhibition (IC50 0.12 µM) without in-vivo or clinical QT prolongation is an in-vitro flag the in-vivo model correctly discounted.

safety.note: Monkey heart-rate fall and delayed respiratory-rate rise at 0.6–2× clinical exposure; clinic saw bradycardia, hypertension and early-onset pulmonary events (6%, median day 2).
safety.short: Lung and heart flagged; early-onset pattern not
safety.quote: Bradycardia, hypertension, and pulmonary toxicity have been observed clinically with brigatinib.
safety.confidence_note: Review read in part (nonclinical summary, safety pharmacology, EOPE case definition). Clinical EOPE numbers are from Kim 2017 (10.1200/JCO.2016.71.5904): 14 of 219 (6%), median onset day 2, none after escalation in the lead-in arm.
safety.magnitude_basis: monkey cardiopulmonary safety pharmacology versus clinical cardiopulmonary adverse events
safety.judgement: Partial, not contra: the review sets monkey cardiopulmonary signs, lung alveolar macrophages and lung/pericardial inflammation deaths beside the clinical pulmonary toxicity, so the species was not silent on the organ. What no animal predicted is the early-onset, first-days pattern that forced the 90 mg lead-in; the review's clinical section says this onset 'has not been described with other ALK' inhibitors. A stricter reading scores that unpredicted pattern contra; the track stays same because the harm itself was flagged.

safety.note: Rat/dog cholesterol rises, dog neuropathy-like signs, lung inflammation and rat memory-recall loss at ≥3 mg/kg preceded clinical hyperlipidaemia (72%), neuropathy, pneumonitis and CNS effects.
safety.quote: The hepatobiliary findings coupled with significant increases in cholesterol (also seen clinically), abdominal distention, and skin findings suggest cholestasis and are included in the label, under Section 13.2.
safety.confidence_note: Review read in part. Clinical rates from Shaw 2017 phase 1: hypercholesterolaemia 72%, hypertriglyceridaemia 39%, peripheral neuropathy 39%, peripheral oedema 39%; the oedema was not found in the animal sections read.
safety.magnitude_basis: rat, dog and safety-pharmacology findings versus labelled warnings
safety.reason: Animal toxicology called the class harms
safety.judgement: The strongest entry on the track: a prospective rat contextual-renewal study (Study 12GR137, pre-first-in-human) found 'clear decreases in memory recall' at ≥3 mg/kg, TRKB inhibition was tied to mood disorders, and the review states 'Clinically, CNS effects including hallucinations, mood disorders, and seizures have occurred'; dogs showed tremor and abnormal gait 'resembling the signs of peripheral neuropathy observed clinically' and lung inflammation while 'pneumonitis occurs clinically'. Peripheral oedema (39%) is the one common harm with no animal flag found; a dog or rat could show it, so a stricter reading records a silent miss, but the review does not call one.
